problemStatement.formal: Survey known bounds and formal placeholders around the minimum size of unavoidable reducible configuration sets used in computer-assisted proofs of the Four Color Theorem.
problemStatement.plain: Record what is known about how small an unavoidable reducible configuration set for the Four Color Theorem can be, including the RSST 633-configuration proof and the lack of a tight lower bound.
whyMatters: Keeps the gallery entry honest about being a survey rather than a new human-readable Four Color proof.
Connects the formal Lean stub to the historical computer-assisted proof strategy.
Separates known configuration counts from the still-open minimality question.

proven: The Robertson-Sanders-Seymour-Thomas proof uses an unavoidable set of 633 reducible configurations.
A lower bound of at least 10 configurations is recorded in the survey entry.
The Lean development contains concrete data types for the survey, but not a full reducibility checker.
open: The exact minimum size of an unavoidable reducible configuration set is not known.
A fully formal, human-readable Four Color proof remains outside this entry.
Bridging the survey data to a verified reducibility-checking pipeline is future work.
knownResults.goal: Represent the minimal-configuration question as a bounded survey entry while keeping the full Four Color proof and reducibility machinery explicitly out of scope.
